title: Postmortem: Regional failover overload causing API SLO misses and emergency load-shedding
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 22:35 UTC a large-scale multi-region event impacted our primary EU region (eu-west-1) routing layer. Automated regional failover moved substantial traffic to NA clusters. Circuit breaker thresholds on several Dedicated pools were conservative and not updated for the increased prefix cache/memory footprint, causing a cascade of slow requests, SLO misses on 99th percentile latency for text-generation endpoints, and emergency load-shedding that impacted ~12% of active customer requests for ~46 minutes. This ticket documents timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations applied, and follow-up action items.
timeline: 2026-03-09 22:32 UTC — EU control-plane spike detected by synthetic probes (1.5x error rate).
2026-03-09 22:35 UTC — Automated routing policy engaged: failover EU -> NA as per multi-region policy. Traffic shift peaked at 22:38 UTC.
2026-03-09 22:40 UTC — NA Dedicated pools reached higher-than-expected memory/KV cache pressure; autoscaler queued scale-ups but new nodes did not register fast enough.
2026-03-09 22:46 UTC — Circuit breaker mTLS health checks tripped for two Dedicated pools due to increased tail latency; fallback invoked to hosted pools.
2026-03-09 22:50 UTC — Load-shedding activated by emergency policy to preserve cluster health; customers experienced 429/503 responses.
2026-03-09 23:20 UTC — Manual intervention: adjusted circuit breaker thresholds, scaled sharding, temporarily increased burst capacity, and reverted routing for critical customers.
2026-03-09 23:22 UTC — Error rate and latency back within SLO window for most traffic; full recovery at 23:28 UTC.
impact_metrics: SLO affected: text-generation latency (99th) target 600ms — observed spike to 2.9s during incident
Customer error rate: 12% of active requests received 429/503 during peak
Duration: ~46 minutes of elevated errors/latency; full recovery by 23:28 UTC
Revenue impact: estimated 0.08% of daily revenue (billing reconciliation in progress)
root_cause: Confluence of events: (1) upstream multi-region routing decision routed high tail-traffic to NA due to eu-west-1 control-plane instability; (2) circuit breaker and health-check thresholds for Dedicated pools were tuned for steady-state, not for rapid cross-region failover bursts; (3) KV cache memory growth and larger-than-expected request fanout per request increased per-instance memory pressure causing slower kernel scheduling and delayed node registration during autoscale; (4) emergency load-shedding policy used a conservative cutoff that prioritized cluster stability but lacked customer-tier-aware exemptions for first-party and high-priority customers.
detection: Incident was detected by synthetic latency probes and on-call alerts from the routing SLO dashboard. Pager fired for SRE rotation at 22:36 UTC. However, dashboards lacked a combined metric showing cross-region traffic shift + per-pool cache pressure which delayed root cause narrowing by ~6 minutes.
mitigation_and_recovery: Applied mitigations in order: (A) Increased Dedicated circuit breaker thresholds and extended health-check grace period to allow nodes to come up during scale events; (B) Manually triggered scale-up of NA pools and increased burst capacity quota; (C) Adjusted routing policy to preserve a small percentage of traffic in EU for rate-limiting variance testing; (D) Applied customer-tier exemptions to load-shedding to avoid 429s for enterprise customers; (E) After stabilization, reverted temporary threshold changes and scheduled controlled rollout of new thresholds.
postmortem_discussion_notes: Design trade-off: current failover policy assumes downstream pools can absorb 2x baseline; real workload had 3.7x effective load due to increased KV cache misses and request multiplication. Consider adding an adaptive throttling window to the failover decision.
Engineering feedback: circuit breakers must be workload-aware not static; introduce per-model and per-customer budgeted headroom metrics.
Product input: customers expect predictable SLAs during region failover; need safer defaults or staged failover with proportional traffic shifts.
Operations: on-call runbooks lacked a single playbook for multi-region failover with Dedicated pools — created new combined runbook.
follow_up_action_items: A1: Implement adaptive failover algorithm to do staged traffic shifting (owner: Liam Chen, due: 2026-04-10)
A2: Update circuit breaker configs to be model- and pool-aware; add automated simulation tests (owner: Mei Rodriguez, due: 2026-03-31)
A3: Add combined metric panel (cross-region traffic shift + per-pool KV cache pressure) and set synthetic alerts (owner: SRE Team, due: 2026-03-24)
A4: Revise load-shedding policy to include customer-tier exemptions and softer degradation modes (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-28)
A5: Increase autoscaler registration timeout and add health-check backoff jitter to prevent thundering during scale-up (owner: Marco Silva, due: 2026-03-22)
A6: Run tabletop exercise for multi-region failover with oncall and platform teams (owner: Aisha Kapoor, due: 2026-04-05)
A7: Post-release audit: verify PR runtime-1.20 includes KB for circuit-breaker tuning (owner: Release Engineering, due: 2026-04-01)
A8: Customer communication: send incident summary to impacted customers + offer SLA credit where applicable (owner: Customer Success, due: 2026-03-16)
A9: Add regression tests to CI that simulate KV-cache blowup under cross-region failover (owner: Test Eng, due: 2026-03-29)
